analysis.title: The Russell Squeeze Is Loaded — And It Won't Take Much
key_insights: The Russell 2000 trend line is holding for now, with the index back above its 200-day moving average, though the report says fragility remains.
Goldman Sachs notes Russell 2000 positioning remains deeply depressed: systematic exposure is in the 7th percentile and leveraged funds hold record shorts per CFTC data through September 22.
Softer PCE and payrolls helped trigger some covering. Around $900mn of open interest has come out since September 29, and RTY funding spreads have richened both outright and versus SPX.
Russell squeezed aggressively during Friday's initial move lower in rates. It held much of that move after yields reversed higher, which opened a short-term divergence versus rates.
The Market Ear's read is that it probably won't take much relief in rates to get Russell squeezing aggressively again. Rates are the trigger.
